blocks.text: This article provides a summary of all new features and enhancements for Authentication Service.
Authentication Service includes the following enhancements:
API clients now support the OAuth 2.1 Authorization Code flow and grant type, enabling applications to securely access Zscaler APIs on behalf of authenticated admins. This enhancement includes:

blocks.item: Support for Client Identity Metadata Documents (CIMD) for client registration
User consent-based authorization with role-based access control (RBAC)
Refresh tokens with rotation during refresh grant
Ability to configure authorization grant duration
OAuth authorization server metadata discovery through the .well-known endpoint to simplify client integration
Centralized management of authorization grants, including the ability to view and revoke active grants

blocks.text: See image.
The existing Client Credentials grant type remains supported. An API client can be configured to use either the Authorization Code or Client Credentials grant type.
You can now configure and manage AI agents that access Zscaler APIs on behalf of authenticated administrators. This enhancement includes:

blocks.item: Predefined AI client configurations for Claude Code and ChatGPT
User consent-based authorization with role-based access control (RBAC)
Audit logging for client management and authorization activities

blocks.text: See image.
To learn more, see About API and AI Agents, Adding an API or AI Agent, and About Authorization Grants.
The Authentication Service pages in the Zscaler Admin Console are updated. The pages are intuitive and visually appealing to improve usability, navigation, and overall user experience.
To learn more, see What is Authentication Service?

blocks.heading: Support for Source IP Addresses and CIDR Ranges in API Client Access Policy

blocks.text: The OneAPI API client access policy framework is extended to support source IP addresses and Classless Inter-Domain Routing (CIDR) ranges as policy criteria. Administrators can select pre-configured trusted IP locations or trusted IP location groups as criteria while configuring the API client access policy rule to restrict specific OneAPI API clients and only accept API requests that originate from approved source IP addresses or CIDR ranges. OneAPI enforces the policy when an assigned API client invokes a Zscaler API.
See image.
To learn more, see About the API Client Access Policy and Adding API Client Access Policy Rule.

Admins can now launch Experience Center tenants for multiple customers from the Partner Portal without logging out from the previously accessed tenant. Experience Center automatically opens the next tenant and maintains only one active browser session for all the accessed tenants.
To learn more, see About Tenants in the Multi-Tenant Portal for Partners.

blocks.heading: Access to Legacy Admin Portals Deprecated

blocks.text: Access to the following Zscaler service Admin Portals is deprecated:
The corresponding legacy Admin Portals tiles are no longer displayed on the Authentication Service single sign-on (SSO) page. Use Experience Center to access these services.

blocks.heading: Unified Role-Based Access Control for Authentication Service

blocks.text: Authentication Service supports Unified Role-Based Access Control (RBAC). Administrators can now view, create, and manage Authentication Service roles centrally on the Role Management page (Administration > Role Management).
See image.
The existing options to configure roles, permissions, and administrative entitlements in Authentication Service are deprecated if you use Unified RBAC.
To access Unified RBAC, contact your Zscaler Account team.
To learn more, see:

You can now configure the password policy to deactivate a user account after a specific number of unsuccessful authentication attempts, and reject a specific number of previously used passwords. You can customize both values from 3 to 10 in the Zscaler Admin Console.
See image.
To learn more, see Configuring the Password Policy.

blocks.heading: Support for Creating Tenants in India Region

blocks.text: Authentication Service now provides support for creating tenants in the India region, in addition to the United States and European Union. To enable connectivity with Authentication Service, make sure to allowlist the required IP ranges in your environment.
To learn more, see Authentication Service Logs.

blocks.heading: Zscaler Cellular Portal Tile Removed from Authentication Service SSO Page

blocks.text: The Zscaler Cellular Portal tile is removed from the Authentication Service single sign-on (SSO) page. You can access Zscaler Cellular from Experience Center.
To learn more, see What is Zscaler Cellular?

Authentication Service is the global and centralized identity management platform for all the Zscaler products. You can now migrate all the users from your external IdPs to Authentication Service. This streamlines the identity management process and eliminates the need to configure the IdP for each Zscaler product separately, and instead manage all the idenitites within Authentication Service. After the migration, end users can authenticate with Authentication Service and access the assigned Zscaler services.
To learn more, see Migrating End Users to Authentication Service.

blocks.heading: Support for NSS Integration with Authentication Service

blocks.text: You can now integrate Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) and Cloud NSS with Authentication Service to stream Authentication Service logs to external security information and event management (SIEM) systems. You can store and monitor the Authentication Service admin audit, authentication, and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) logs.
See image.
To learn more, see About Log Streaming.

blocks.heading: Support for Integrating Two Private Access Tenants

blocks.text: Authentication Service provides support for integrating two Private Access (ZPA) tenants at a time. This allows customers to manage multiple tenants through the Zscaler Admin Console. The following authentication scenarios are supported for Private Access tenants:
For admins:

blocks.item: Identity provider (IdP)-initiated single-sign on (SSO) to access all tenants from Authentication Service.
Service provider-initiated SSO for all tenants.
Access tenants by logging in to the Zscaler Admin Console.

blocks.text: For users:

blocks.item: Zscaler Client Connector enrollment for Private Access tenants.

blocks.text: To learn more, see Customizing Your Account Settings and Multiple Private Access Tenant Support with Authentication Service.

For new deployments, Authentication Service now provides support for end users. Admins can manage a single identity for end users across all Zscaler services. End users have an improved user experience, as Zscaler Client Connector enrollment is faster, and they can securely log in once and access any of the assigned Zscaler services.
Authentication Service for end users centralizes user identity administration and enables new adaptive access use cases with Step-Up Authentication and the Adaptive Access Engine.
End user support for existing customers is coming soon.
To learn more, see What is Authentication Service?

You can now integrate Nanolog Streaming Service (NSS) and Cloud NSS with Authentication Service to stream Authentication Service logs to external security information and event management (SIEM) systems. You can store and monitor the Authentication Service admin audit, authentication, and System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) logs.
To enable the Log Streaming feature, contact Zscaler Support.
See image.
To learn more, see About Log Streaming.

blocks.heading: OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials Authentication for SCIM Provisioning

blocks.text: Authentication Service provides support to use OAuth 2.0 Client Credentials for authentication while configuring SCIM provisioning with external identity providers (IdPs).
See image.

blocks.heading: Integration of Management Portal for Partners with Authentication Service

blocks.text: The Zscaler Management Portal for Partners is now integrated with Authentication Service. You can enable single sign-on (SSO) for partner logins and provide a unified authentication experience. You can assign roles and scopes to partner users migrated to Authentication Service from the Administrative Entitlements page.
See image.
To learn more, see Assigning Entitlements to Users and User Groups.
